_README: Copy to vault/settings/signal.json and REPLACE THE PLACEHOLDERS. vault/ is never committed.
*** THIS FILE IS YOURS AND NOBODY ELSE'S. ***
It is the vocabulary the radar uses to guess which roles you might want read first. Every
line in it is a statement about YOU: what you do, what you will not do, and what you have
already ruled out. It lived in tools/radar/radar.py until 2026-08-26, which meant one
person's preferences shipped to everyone who cloned this repo -- a florist got a scale
built for a delivery director, and a data-centre engineer got a -6 for their own career.
🔴 THE TIER IS A READING HINT, NOT A RANKING, AND NOT A FILTER.
Everything that clears the location filter and the avoid list is listed in the shortlist
whatever it scores here. Measured on a real run: a tally of 13 covered roles later assessed
at anywhere from 6 to 15 out of 15 on the actual scoring framework, and three roles the user
had already APPLIED FOR scored 6, 8 and 10. The tally measures how closely an advert's
WORDING matches these words. It does not measure whether the job suits you.
LEAVING THIS FILE OUT IS A VALID CHOICE. With no signal.json the radar tiers nothing,
excludes nothing on title, and lists every role that passed the real filters. That is
Patterns are regular expressions, matched case-insensitively against the title and the
description together. Keep them short. 'why' is for you, and is never read by the code.

thresholds._comment: Above 'high' is worth reading first; above 'med' is worth reading. Nothing is dropped.

positive.match: <a technology or practice central to your work>
positive.why: <why a role mentioning this is likely to suit you>

positive.match: <a phrase that would only appear in a role you want>
positive.why: <the rarer and more specific, the higher the weight is worth>

negative.match: <work you do not want to do>
negative.why: <state it plainly -- this is the half people leave vague and regret>

negative.match: <an adjacent industry whose listings keep matching your words>
negative.why: <the domains that recur and are reliably wrong for you>

negative.match: <a working pattern you will not accept>

_comment: Whole words matched against the TITLE only. A role whose title contains one is not
listed at all -- this is the one part of this file that does drop a role, so keep it
to things you are certain about.
🔴 One person's exclusion is another's profession. Do not copy somebody else's list.
words: <a trade or profession that is definitely not yours>

_comment: Titles that describe doing the work rather than leading it. Excluded from the shortlist.
🔴 If you ARE an individual contributor, LEAVE THIS EMPTY -- otherwise the tool hides
every role you want. It exists because a second-line manager kept being shown
engineer-level roles, and that is a fact about that person, not about the market.
A title matches when it is (optional seniority) + (optional domain) + one of the nouns.
